population.definition: Banjul Local Government Area (Banjul City Council), the island city, 2013 census, both sexes

facts.claim: On 23 April 1816 Captain Alexander Grant made a treaty with the king of Kombo, Tomani Bojang, leasing the island to the British for 103 iron bars a year.

source.title: Banjul History
source.quote: On the 23rd April 1816 Captain Alexander Grant entered into a treaty with Tomani Bojang

facts.claim: The lease was paid as a yearly sum of 103 iron bars.

source.title: Banjul History
source.quote: yearly payment of 103 iron bars

facts.claim: The settlement was named Bathurst after the British Colonial Secretary, and the island before 1816 was known to the Portuguese as Banjulo.

source.title: The Gambia - Slave Trade
source.quote: Originally called Banjulo by the Portuguese, Grant named the new settlement, Bathurst after the Colonial Secretary of the time Lord Bathurst.

source.title: Banjul History
source.quote: In 1973 Bathurst was re-named Banjul

facts.claim: In the 1980s, after a period of stagnation, many residents left Banjul for the Kombos, creating the Greater Banjul area.

source.title: Banjul History
source.quote: After a period of stagnation and decay in the 1980's the capital saw a rapid exodus of much of the population from Banjul

facts.claim: In the 2013 census Banjul had the smallest share of the national population of any local government area, 1.6 percent.

source.title: Population Distribution: 5 Observations
source.quote: Banjul accounting for the lowest proportion of the population (1.6 percent)

facts.claim: Banjul had the lowest share of females of any local government area in 2013, at 48.9 percent.

source.title: Population Distribution: 5 Observations
source.quote: has the lowest proportion of females across all the LGAs at 48.9 percent

facts.claim: Banjul municipality is the seat of government of The Gambia.

source.title: The Gambia Demographic and Health Survey 2013
source.quote: Banjul municipality (the seat of the government)

facts.claim: Banjul and Kanifing are entirely urban, with no rural strata, in the 2013 survey design.

source.title: The Gambia Demographic and Health Survey 2013
source.quote: except Banjul and Kanifing, which are entirely urban settlements

facts.claim: Comparing the 2013 and 2024 censuses, Banjul was the only local government area whose population declined (by 15 percent).

source.title: Factsheet: Almost half of Gambians live in Brikama Local Government Area
source.quote: Banjul was the only region where the population declined (-15%)

facts.claim: The Gambia Ports Authority took over cargo handling in the port of Banjul from 1 January 1973.

source.title: The Gambia Ports Authority At 50 (1972-2022): Some Milestones
source.quote: took over full control of all cargo handling operation in the port of Banjul with effect from 1st January 1973

facts.claim: The museum's ground floor is dedicated to an exhibition on Banjul's history called 'Banjul, Bathurst, Banjul'.

source.title: National Museum of The Gambia
source.quote: became a space for the »Banjul, Bathurst, Banjul« exhibition, telling a story about The Gambia's capital

timeline.claim: Portuguese navigators entered the mouth of the Gambia River in 1455 and were driven off by hostile locals.

source.title: Banjul History
source.quote: entered the mouth of the Gambia River in 1455 before being ejected by hostile locals

timeline.claim: Captain Alexander Grant concluded a treaty with Tomani Bojang, king of Kombo, for the island on 23 April 1816.

source.title: Banjul History
source.quote: On the 23rd April 1816 Captain Alexander Grant entered into a treaty with Tomani Bojang

timeline.claim: The name Bathurst symbolised British colonial rule over the island from 1816 to 1965.

source.title: National Museum of The Gambia
source.quote: that name became a symbol of the British colonial rule over it from 1816 to 1965

timeline.claim: The Gambia Ports Authority began operating on 1 July 1972.

source.title: The Gambia Ports Authority At 50 (1972-2022): Some Milestones
source.quote: The Gambia Ports Authority commenced operation on 1st July 1972

source.title: Banjul History
source.quote: In 1973 Bathurst was re-named Banjul

timeline.claim: The National Museum was created in 1985 by the first ministry of culture.

source.title: National Museum of The Gambia
source.quote: In 1985 the National museum was created by the first ministry of culture

timeline.claim: Arch 22 was built between 1995 and 1996 at a cost of US$1 million.

source.title: Time for the truth in Gambia
source.quote: was built between 1995 and 1996, costing taxpayers US$1 million

timeline.claim: The 2013 census counted 31,054 people in Banjul.
After the fall of Yahya Jammeh in January 2017 the 'unknown soldier' statue from Arch 22 was removed and later relocated to the National Museum.

source.title: Time for the truth in Gambia
source.quote: The ‘unknown soldier’ was removed by a group of civilian vigilantes after the fall of Jammeh in January 2017

places.name: Kunta Kinteh Island
places.what: Kunta Kinteh Island, formerly James Island, lies in the River Gambia and is a UNESCO World Heritage site with related sites. UNESCO describes it as a testimony to the encounter between Africa and Europe and links it to the beginning and abolition of the slave trade.

facts.label: Significance
facts.value: Testimony to the main periods of the Africa-Europe encounter along the River Gambia

source.title: The Slaves Hunter's Island: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites
source.quote: present a testimony to the main periods and facets of the encounter between Africa and Europe along the River Gambia

facts.label: Slave trade
facts.value: Particularly significant for the beginning of the slave trade and its abolition

source.title: The Slaves Hunter's Island: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites
source.quote: particularly significant for its relation to the beginning of the slave trade and its abolition

source.title: The Slaves Hunter's Island: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites
source.quote: Kunta Kinteh Island (formerly James Island)

facts.label: Literary fame
facts.value: James Island and Juffure became famous through Alex Haley's Roots (1976)

source.title: The Gambia - Slave Trade
source.quote: James Island and Juffure became famous when Alex Haley chronicled his ancestor, Kunta Kinteh

facts.label: Erosion
facts.value: The 17th-century fort is in danger of collapsing as the shoreline erodes

source.title: National Museum of The Gambia
source.quote: is in danger of collapsing since the island's shoreline proceeds to erode

places.name: Albert Market
places.what: Albert Market is on Liberation Avenue and is the capital's main urban market. It is named after Prince Albert, the husband of Queen Victoria.

source.title: Albert Market - Banjul
source.quote: Albert Market is in Banjul on Liberation Avenue and is the capital's main urban market

facts.label: Named after
facts.value: Prince Albert, husband of Queen Victoria

source.title: Albert Market - Banjul
source.quote: It was named after Queen Victoria's husband Prince Albert Saxe-Coburg and Gotha

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Liberation Avenue, a few metres from the river bank

source.title: Albert Market - Banjul
source.quote: The river bank is only a few metres away behind Albert Market

places.name: Arch 22
places.what: Arch 22 is a monument at the entrance to Banjul, made a national monument in 2000. It was built in 1995-1996 and today shows exhibitions in its upper floors.

facts.label: Size
facts.value: Three floors, 42 m high and 30 m wide

source.title: Time for the truth in Gambia
source.quote: The imposing three-floor structure — 42 metres high and 30 metres wide — was built between 1995 and 1996

source.title: Time for the truth in Gambia
source.quote: was built between 1995 and 1996, costing taxpayers US$1 million

source.title: Time for the truth in Gambia
source.quote: In 2000, the Arch – widely called “Arch 22” – was made a national monument

facts.label: Exhibitions
facts.value: Shows pictures both celebrating Jammeh's rule and depicting its human rights violations

source.title: Time for the truth in Gambia
source.quote: the Arch already exhibits pictures both celebrating Jammeh’s rule and depicting its human rights violations

places.name: National Museum of The Gambia
places.what: The National Museum stands on Independence Drive in Banjul and was created in 1985. Its ground floor tells the story of Banjul in the exhibition 'Banjul, Bathurst, Banjul'.

source.title: The Gambia National Museum
source.quote: Established in 1985

source.title: The Gambia National Museum
source.quote: Location: Independence Drive, PMB 151, Banjul, The Gambia

facts.label: Exhibition
facts.value: 'Banjul, Bathurst, Banjul' on the ground floor

source.title: National Museum of The Gambia
source.quote: became a space for the »Banjul, Bathurst, Banjul« exhibition, telling a story about The Gambia's capital

source.title: National Museum of The Gambia
source.quote: revitalised and updated in 2003
